report.md:
## This week

You posted 12 videos this week. Your views went down from last week. Last week your typical video got about 2,472 views. This week it dropped to about 1,838 views.

Your best video was the one that starts with "First I went to TikTok and looked up U.G.C." It pulled in 12,100 views. That is huge for you.

Your weakest was the one that starts with "One of the most freeing things was realizing that I can literally just leave." It only got 1,217 views. You also posted three brand new videos in the last day, so it is too soon to judge those. Give them time.

## Is it how you film, or what you say?

Right now, almost every single video you post is you talking to camera. That means you have not really tested other filming styles enough to know if they help or hurt. What you have tested more is what you talk about, and that is showing a clearer pattern than how you film it.

Your best video this week was about how UGC really works. That topic is doing well overall too, not just this once. Your weakest video this week was your big picture money talk. That topic tends to run below your usual views across the board.

I do not have any cases this week where you filmed the same script two different ways, so I cannot fully separate "how you film" from "what you say" yet. What I can tell you is this: right now, topic seems to matter more than filming style, but you have not given filming style a fair test.

## What is working

Your how you got started videos usually pull about twice your normal views. You have posted 22 of them, so this is a real pattern.

Your real money numbers videos are doing even better, about three and a half times your normal views. You have posted 7 of these, so it is a smaller group but still worth paying attention to.

Videos with a link in bio call to action are pulling way above normal, but you have only posted 6 of them, so treat that as promising, not proven.

## Try this next week

Film one more how you got started video, since that topic keeps outperforming everything else.

Try telling a real money numbers story but in a totally different filming style, like voice over footage or a photo carousel, so you can finally tell if the style helps or if it was always the topic.

Skip the big picture money talk topic for now, or pair it with a stronger topic like how you got started, since on its own it keeps underperforming.

best.md:
This video did well. It pulled in about three times the views a normal video of yours gets.

Your opening line was "First I went to TikTok and looked up U.G.C." That's a says the value up front hook, and it works here because you're promising a clear process right away. It tells people exactly what they're about to get, which earns those first few seconds.

After that, the video kept giving people a reason to stay. You laid out each step in order: research, find examples, use Canva, copy the video, apply on Kora and Reddit. That step by step structure keeps people watching because they want the next step.

There was no call to action in this video. That's a missed chance. With this many people watching, you could have asked them to comment their biggest UGC question, or told them to follow for the next video on landing deals.

Next time, add a call to action partway through, right after you give the Canva tip, since that's a natural moment where people are already hooked and still watching.

worst.md:
This video did badly. It got 1,217 views, well under what a normal video of yours gets, which is 3,806.

Your opening line was "One of the most freeing things was realizing that I can literally just leave." It sets up a contradiction, which usually works, but here the "zoom out business" style videos with this hook only pull in about 2,642 to 3,170 views most of the time. So even the format was working against you a bit.

After that opening, the video stays on one idea the whole time. You explain what you mean by "leave," but you don't add a new twist or turn to keep people hooked past the first few seconds. It plays like one thought, said once, in twelve seconds.

There was no call to action. You could have asked people to comment on what they need to "leave" behind, or told them to follow for more mindset thoughts like this one.

Next time, add a second beat after your opening line, something that complicates or builds on the first thought, so people have a reason to keep watching past second six.
